newsitem.title: GERMANY: Compaq sees German market share fall.
newsitem.headline: Compaq sees German market share fall.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp said on Thursday its German unit lost two points of market share in the face of sharp price competition in 1996.
Compaq Computer GmbH had market share of 7.8 percent in 1996 and shipped just over 300,000 personal computers, the company said, quoting figures from market researcher Dataquest.
But its share fell in three out of four market segments in Germany, Compaq said.

Compaq's share of home PC sales fell to 3.5 percent, from 7.5 percent in 1995. In sales to businesses, its share slipped to 12.9 percent from 13.3 percent, and in portable PCs its share dropped to 14.7 percent from 16 percent.
Its only increase came in the server segment, where its share rose to 25.6 percent from 24.7 percent.
The total German market grew 11 percent to a 3.86 million PCs, with sales to mid-sized companies rising 21 percent and sales to large corporations increasing 15 percent, Compaq said.

Home PC sales, hit by Germany's weak economy, rose only one percent. Compaq's rank in the home market fell to number 11, down from number three in 1995. Vobis Microcomputer AG was Germany's top seller of home PCs.
Compaq was hurt because it had few products selling for less than 3,000 marks, Kurt Dobitsch, the company's top executive in Germany said.
